title: memory/candidates/<id>.json — a candidate memory
description: Written by core/memory/candidates.js. ⛔ A CANDIDATE IS NOT A FACT. `verificationState` is the wall: only a `verified` record may be promoted to canonical project memory (memory/graph/<type>/<slug>.md, per memory/knowledge-graph.md's file-backed schema), promotion requires at least one supporting evidence path, and a `candidate` may only ever be recalled as an unverified lead. The record is REWRITTEN as its state changes and the append-only memory/candidates/audit.jsonl beside it is the authority for how it got there — the opposite trade from the rollover handoff, whose bytes are the evidence and which is therefore never rewritten. TRACKED, not runtime: candidates are project knowledge-in-waiting, evaluated and promoted or rejected by an explicit, audited human/agent decision. This is core/'s own normative copy of the RECORD branch of schemas/candidate-memory.schema.json, which is the file schemas/registry.json resolves; the two are kept STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL (required fields, property types, enums) rather than one deferring to a path the other cannot resolve, since registry entries resolve schema files under schemas/ and core/ may not require anything outside itself. The store's DIRECTORY is the caller's, not this schema's: core/memory/candidates.js appends a `memory` leaf to a conversation directory by default and takes an exact directory via `storeDir({dir})`, which is how kernel/respawnpack.js places the project-wide store at memory/candidates/.

claim.description: The assertion, as captured. A memory with no assertion asserts nothing and cannot be checked.

klass.description: Only these four may ever become canonical. Anything else is a note, and notes do not become project truth.

cycleId.description: WHICH CONTEXT CYCLE produced it. Required: a memory outlives the cycle that made it, and one that cannot name that cycle cannot be audited against what was known then. For a kernel-CLI capture (savepoint has no rollover-machine cycle of its own), this is the git revision the candidate was captured at.

evidencePaths.description: Paths, never conclusions. An empty array is a real answer and is exactly what blocks promotion.

previousState.description: A VERIFIED memory may be rejected later; findings are overturned. The prior state is kept so the audit shows what was believed and for how long.
